question: catch
message: Catch-only methods assume the catch series is complete. Under-reported or missing catches bias productivity and depletion directly.

question: goal
message: Catch-only status is driven largely by priors on depletion and resilience. It should not be the sole basis for catch advice.

question: lifehistory
message: Short-lived, recruitment-driven stocks fluctuate strongly; catch-only depletion priors are rarely informative for them.

question: catch
message: Surplus production models treat catch as (near) complete removals. Reconstruct missing catches or add catch uncertainty before fitting.

question: index_length
message: A short index relative to the catch history weakly identifies depletion and productivity. Use informative priors and test initial-depletion sensitivity.

question: index_type
message: Commercial CPUE may be hyperstable or affected by changing targeting. Standardise it (see cpueTargeting) before use.

question: species
message: Single-species production models ignore technical interactions; reference points may not be jointly achievable in mixed fisheries.

question: gears
message: Single-fleet length methods assume one selectivity. Pooling gears with different selectivity biases SPR; use a multi-gear model (FLicc, fishblicc) or analyse gears separately.

question: dynamics
message: Equilibrium per-recruit methods lag behind changes in F or recruitment: pessimistic during a rebuild, optimistic while F increases.

question: lh
message: Results are most sensitive to Linf and M/k. Life-history proxies (e.g. from FishBase) require sensitivity runs over plausible ranges.

question: length
message: Check sample size per gear-year: fewer than about 50 fish or 10 length bins is a red flag. Pool or drop poorly sampled years.

question: goal
message: Length-based per-recruit methods give status relative to F reference points, not biomass or catch levels. Catch advice needs an additional step (e.g. an indicator-based HCR).

question: species
message: Single-stock per-recruit reference points ignore technical interactions between species caught together.

question: goal
message: An assessment fit alone does not test a harvest control rule. Use the assessment as the estimation model in an MSE (see FLR mse).
